full_judgment:
2. Sonali Bank the respondent No.2 as the plaintiff' instituted Title Suit No. 1 of 1998 for realization of Tk. 9,42,866.21 impleading the present defendant. The suit was decreed on contest. Thereafter the bank put the decree into execution being Title Execution Case No.8 of 2000. In the execution proceeding the present-petitioner, the judgment-debtor, filed an application for stay of the execution proceeding under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the ground that the judgment-debtor had also obtained a decree against the respondent No.2 Bank for an amount of Tk.15,45,002/-. The Artha Rin Adalat after hearing the decree holder and judgment-debtor rejected the application by impugned order dated 19.08.2001. 

 3. Mr. Md. Harunur Rashid, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submitted that the High Court Division ought to have found that the petitioner obtained decree in Money Suit No.1 of 1997 against respondent No.2-Bank for Tk.15,45,002/- which is under challenge and respondent No.2-Bank obtained decree in Title Suit No.1 of 1998 against the petitioners for Tk. 9,42,866.21 paisa which is not under challenge due to subsection 2 of section 7 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 and if Bank succeeds in appeal there is no bar to realize the decreetal amount and until disposal of the appeal the respondent No.2 Bank can not start the execution proceeding and put in auction the property for sale and the impugned judgment and order offends against the guarantee of right to property given by the Constitution The learned Advocate further submitted that the High Court Division committed serious error of law in discharging the rule ignoring the fact that the decree of civil court in both the suits are binding upon the parties and the High Court Division ought to have given a direction to the respondent No.2 to the effect that let the appeal be disposed of within two months meanwhile execution proceeding may be stayed. 

 "The respondent bank obtained the decree from the jurisdiction of the Artha Rin Adalat and the judgment debtor the present petitioner obtained the decree against the bank from ordinary civil court and that decree is now the subject matter of appeal pending before this court, pendency of the appeal cannot be the ground for stay of the execution proceeding pending in the court of Artha Rin Adalat. From the impugned order does not seem to was that the Artha Rin Adalat passed the order without having jurisdiction or that the Adalat acted in excess of its jurisdiction. The writ petition is otherwise also not maintainable." 

 5. It is true that the petitioners obtained a decree against the present plaintiff for Tk.15,45,002/- which is more than the amount claimed by the present respondent in its suit but the above decree is under-challenge. In the instant case, only an appeal under section 7(2) could be preferred' challenging the decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and in the absence of any such appeal, we do not find that the petitioner's application for stay of the Artha Rin Execution Case No.2 of 2001 is maintainable. If in the petitioners suit the decree is maintained finally the petitioner can get the decree executed in accordance with law but under the provision of Artha Rin Adalat the proceeding in the execution case can not be stayed.
